summary.intent: Implement SDK-based E2E and load test infrastructure for CipherBox, replacing browser-dependent Playwright tests with direct SDK calls for both correctness testing and high-volume load testing.
summary.outcome: Created two new workspace packages (tests/sdk-e2e with 83 passing tests across 10 suites, tests/load with 5 load scenarios), a throttle bypass mechanism for test environments, two CI workflows, and a testing strategy document. All 83 SDK E2E tests pass locally against real API/IPFS/Postgres stack.

repo: setApiClientConfig is a module-level singleton used by orval-generated functions in sdk-core — all multi-account tests must call setApiClientConfig before each operation that uses the API, causing cross-suite contamination if not reset
The API throttler (10 req/s, 100 req/min) applies per-controller via @UseGuards(ThrottlerGuard), not globally — each controller import must be swapped individually
NODE_ENV in .env file takes precedence over shell env vars because NestJS ConfigModule loads .env first, overriding process.env values passed to the child process
The /auth/test-login endpoint returns { accessToken, refreshToken, isNewUser, publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex } and has its own stricter throttle (5 per 15 min)
ClaimInviteDto has @MinLength(258) on encryptedKey — requires at least 258 hex chars (129 bytes), meaning dummy byte arrays of 64 bytes fail validation
pnpm workspace new packages need pnpm install run at the root to wire up symlinks before TypeScript can resolve workspace: protocol dependencies
The pre-commit hook regenerates the API client when api-client source files change — modifying instance.ts requires running pnpm api:generate before committing
crypto.getRandomValues() has a 65,536 byte hard limit per call — generating files larger than 64KB requires chunked calls

code.finding: Module-level _config singleton shared by all orval-generated functions — no instance scoping possible without refactoring orval codegen config and threading axios instance through sdk-core's SdkContext
Gold standard test-login → initializeVault → encryptVaultKeys → setApiClientConfig → CipherBoxClient pattern for SDK test setup
ThrottlerModule configured with ttl:60000/limit:100 and ttl:1000/limit:10 — must be conditionally relaxed or bypassed for test environments

workflow: For NestJS dev server, env vars injected in shell don't override .env file values — must edit the .env file directly or use a separate .env.test file
sed replace-all for adding function wrappers around object literals (e.g., headers: { to headers: fn({) requires paired closing paren fixes — easier to rewrite the file directly
Vitest with fileParallelism:false still shares the Node.js module cache between test files, so module-level singletons like setApiClientConfig bleed across suites — later suites must re-set them
Promise.allSettled swallows rejection reasons silently — load test scenarios need explicit logging of result.reason to surface workload errors
noUnusedLocals in tsconfig causes TS errors on unused imports from test setup — prefix with _ or remove imports rather than leaving them

friction: 1Password SSH agent unavailable in agent subprocesses — git commits requiring SSH signing hung indefinitely, required user to commit from terminal or retry
sed-based bulk replacements of headers: { → headers: fetchHeaders({ left mismatched closing parens, corrupting vault-lifecycle.test.ts and requiring a full rewrite
The 'simplify' review phase discovered and fixed issues (getRawSamples copy, setApiClientConfig re-use, folderTree as any) that should have been caught during initial implementation
Throttle 429s appeared even with NODE_ENV=test conditional because IPNS publish endpoints have their own @Throttle decorators that ignore the module-level limit change
noUnusedLocals TS errors required multiple rounds of fixes after initial Write calls — should have checked tsconfig strictness settings before writing test files
Background bash tasks with long git signing waits needed explicit TaskOutput polling to determine status, adding latency to the commit workflow
open_items: Refactor api-client from module-level singleton to instance-scoped axios: configure orval to generate functions accepting an axios instance parameter, thread through sdk-core SdkContext, have CipherBoxClient own its axios instance — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-refactor-api-client-from-singleton-to-instance-scoped-axios.md

Migrate raw fetch() calls in vault-lifecycle.test.ts, share-operations.test.ts, invite-link.test.ts to use orval-generated API client functions — currently uses testFetch() workaround that can be deleted after singleton refactor

Load test error resilience: concurrent IPNS publishes from multiple clients hit sequence number conflicts (expected behavior) but the error categorization doesn't distinguish throttle 429s from sequence conflicts — add error type breakdown to metrics reporter
Load test scenarios need a 'throttle validation' scenario that runs WITHOUT bypass header to verify the throttler fires correctly under expected load — important for staging health checks
The testFetch() helper, fetchHeaders export, and setApiClientConfig re-set in error-cases.test.ts are all temporary workarounds that become dead code after the singleton refactor
CI sdk-e2e.yml workflow needs THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET added to the GitHub repository secrets before the workflow can run successfully in CI

Load test 429s on IPNS publish endpoint during upload-throughput (37/60 succeed with 3 clients) — investigate whether per-endpoint @Throttle decorators are bypassed by BypassableThrottlerGuard or if they use a separate guard instance
